recorded_boundaries.text: This is the setting of the manuscript theorem; it is not a finite-instance algorithmic runtime guarantee.
The extensive uncut Hamiltonian need not have an operator limit. Smallness of a generator on a core alone is not the needed exponential or domain statement.

The proof first fixes outer Lipschitz constants, then inner errors, using seed truncation, the regularized inverse sine, cutoffs and Fourier approximation. Approximation is in the rooted L² norm, not merely in marginal distribution.
This query root keeps the fixed-minimizer hypothesis in scope and exposes the complete conditional scalar-to-rooted construction. It is not a declaration that a minimizer exists.

Closed witness application: attainment supplies gamma in the manuscript class U, and the universally quantified fixed-minimizer construction uses that same gamma before any finite choices are frozen. Its annotated support edge exposes the conditional argument while discharging the supplied manuscript admissibility and minimizer premises only within this use. The binding is authored source correspondence, not mechanically checked witness equality or proof acceptance.
Disjoint mask orthogonality and the Gaussian isometry control the loss. Shared descendant branches are not assumed independent. Uniform derivative bounds refer to the original grouped coordinates.
Both norm convergence and the occupation bound are hypotheses. Strong convergence or one-point distributional convergence by itself does not permit multiplying an edge correlation by √D.
Equality of seed marginals or ordinary Gram convergence does not alone prove rooted energy convergence. The displayed L-pairing calculation is a separate ingredient.
BFMVZ Theorem 1 is a fixed-depth, fixed-angle identity. It does not transfer raw seeded, masked or controlled words, give a joint n,p,D limit, or certify the construction preceding seed removal.

Measurable seed masks are permitted through bounded subsequences with Gaussian almost-everywhere convergence. Grouped finite control coordinates are essential; no dimension-free assertion is made for all flattened color coordinates.

The receiving root seed is independent of these child fields. The first-chaos identity is an identity in the shared rooted space; a marginal Gaussian law alone does not identify E(v). This is a manuscript construction, not a Lean declaration.

First fix the finite input channels and surrounding word. Helper pinning concerns all helper descendants, not only the receiver root. Individual approximating commutator factors need not preserve that subspace. Lower first responses and scalar second responses must be retained; covariance between channels cannot be discarded.

This is finite approximation of selected local rooted operations. It is not a uniform global operator-norm Trotter estimate on an extensive Hamiltonian, and no error may be multiplied by a growing vertex count.

The finite word and all angles are held fixed before D→∞. Rotated axes and a seed gate exp(−it Zs) have the corresponding rooted formulas; this calculation alone is not a transfer theorem for seeded words.

This is an existence statement for one common finite word. Cost gates, mixers, identity padding and combining adjacent equal gate types convert it to the standard alternating QAOA convention. The tree-to-SK step is still a separate theorem.
The exponential statement has its own domain and weighted Gronwall argument. It is not inferred solely from a small Hilbert–Schmidt kernel or small generator.

This realizes both the finite scalar joint law and its shifted energy pairing. It does not assert strong finite-degree convergence for the unsmoothed sign formula. Intermediate transmitted columns need not be bounded.
The full displaced packets may have occupation of order r^(−2); only their tails have uniform weighted bounds. No uniform whole-packet occupation bound is imported from the finite-word degree limit.

Some ordinary angles are of order 1/r and can be very large, but are finite before any degree or system-size limit. The theorem gives no bound on word length, angle size or an efficient search procedure.

The same vertex seed is reused in every seed gate. Compilation proceeds outer rank to inner rank: pointwise approximants, sender partitions, finite commutators, then lower ranks; raw-seed masks are compiled last. No uniformity as helper probabilities vanish or circuit length grows is claimed.
One must prove the net o(r) cancellation. Replacing a moving insertion by an O(r)-accurate approximation and subsequently multiplying that error by 1/r is not valid.
The word is finite after the projection list is fixed. This is exact finite-list ensemble control of limiting packet data, not a uniform control statement over a continuum of unknown centers.
The order is terminal cutoff, finite scalar mesh, then finite smoothing. The statement has no joint-limit or uniform-in-terminal-time rate and still allows unbounded intermediate columns.

The displacement limit uses the o(r) error and the actual insertion change. Norm remainders are transported through unitaries; an unbounded observable is not applied to an uncontrolled norm remainder.
No maximizer of the noncompact angle supremum is required; no exact optimality at finite depth is inferred.

The construction must not choose a list from its own as-yet-unproved small-r limit. The perturbation preserves the target energy by continuity; it supplies finite nonvanishing conditions, not a uniform numerical lower bound over all words.

Uniformity concerns a fixed finite calculation, bounded parameter sets and specified weighted norms. It does not imply global operator-norm convergence, a nondegenerate covariance assumption, or uniformity in growing word length.

Manuscript-level claim with system size tending to infinity first and circuit depth then increasing; finite deterministic angles depend on the desired accuracy and are independent of system size and disorder. No quantitative finite-size estimate, depth bound, or efficient angle-selection procedure is claimed. The whole manuscript argument has not been independently reviewed here and has no retained Lean circuit-convergence target.
This is a conditional expectation identity, not a claim that F_N equals the terminal gradient pointwise. Independence and the bound |u|≤1 are essential.
Control is in growing-dimensional ell², not only coordinatewise. The rounding-coordinate boundary term A_N B_{N+1} is retained until shown to vanish.
T is fixed first. Normalizers are eventually positive uniformly over active indices, not asserted positive for all meshes. The g_j have no sqrt(Δ) factor; that factor enters M_N=∑sqrt(Δ)g_j/c_j.
The terminal formula subtracts the full integral, whereas P(gamma) subtracts half. The proof uses U₁X₁=|X₁| and does not require P(X₁=0)=0 or a pointwise sign assertion at zero.

The exhibiting lower-bound proof supplies attainment, although Theorem 1 displays an infimum. Use when choosing a minimizer; do not add as a premise of a conditional theorem about every given minimizer.

External mathematical input to the manuscript value identification. The headline theorem is about the almost-sure limit; expectation identification also uses Gaussian concentration/uniform integrability as described in the support manuscript footnote. It is not a retained Lean-replay result.

The sum is shifted: B_{j+1}, including the final rounding coordinate. N is mesh count, distinct from spin-system size n. No circuit, efficient computation, convergence rate, uniform terminal estimate, or prescribed diagonal N(T) is supplied by this proposition.
Uses a=Phi_xx≥0, E a²=1, and P_*=∫₀¹E a. This quantitative bound is present in the manuscript; the exported FiniteGaussianConclusion promises terminal convergence rather than this inequality.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Requires the terminal smoothing constraint ci<=M and monotone coefficient jumps. Source-level maximum-principle/radial-lift argument retained as a package, with its boundary controls explicitly supplied by differentiated tails.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Compact mass removal covers atomic, diffuse and singular continuous measures. It needs only local finiteness, not finite total mass. Minimality is a premise of the conditional result, not an independently supplied existence theorem. The minimizer premise here belongs to the ordinary manuscript model; formal-interface hypotheses remain on the separate Lean target. This classification does not prove a transport between formal models. Global scaling gamma_epsilon=(1-epsilon)gamma is another proof of the same result. Signed Fubini follows from integral gamma|q-t|<=integral gamma<infinity, even for infinite total Stieltjes mass. Both local and global proofs use the same feasible L1 first variation.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. No slope condition at time 1 is available. For an initial gap with 0 outside S, the later argument uses q(0)=0 without assuming contact at 0. The minimizer premise here belongs to the ordinary manuscript model; formal-interface hypotheses remain on the separate Lean target. This classification does not prove a transport between formal models.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Same Brownian system, coefficient and control value throughout; uniqueness permits later transfer of moment identities to any associated diffusion. Pathwise coupling and existence are source-level analytic packages, not an observed build.

An ordinary one-dimensional calculus lemma with its own quantified hypotheses. It applies to toy curves as well as diffusion moments and carries no minimizer, PDE or stochastic premise. Strict convexity gives q′(t) below its endpoint chord for r<t<s; the chord is at most one, and continuity makes the integrated deficit strictly positive. The source uses this step inside a conditional full-support argument. This node does not assert a newly extracted Lean declaration or independently accepted formal check.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. The full real-parameter one-sided derivative is the manuscript statement. The cited Lean declaration records a sampled chord limit and the resulting variational inequality; it is not asserted to have the identical type. A coefficient-convexity/Lipschitz bridge can relate these analytic statements, but no new Lean theorem is claimed.

Authored fixed-time consequence of smooth finite-step coercivity and compact-strip spatial-moment convergence. The ordinary proof flattens gamma locally; the inspected SKSupport source instead uses sampled jets along its canonical diffusion. actual_coercivity takes t:Time with 0<t and ContinuousAt gamma.val t and proves the scaled c^4/c^2 polynomial inequality. Its type does not require c>0; positivity is needed here to divide by c^2. This source correspondence does not identify the SKSupport and SKValue models, pass third time derivatives through a shrinking-plateau limit, or establish the smooth-density corollary as an exported formal conclusion. No fresh Lean build, elaborated dependency extraction, Comparator result or independent semantic acceptance is recorded.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. The zero-flux conclusion is analytic. It is not implied by a symbolic polynomial identity; both signs and vanishing boundary flux are required. These auxiliary profiles are not asserted to converge for general gamma.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. The manuscript variable j is not the Lean Wronskian r*s_x-s*r_x=r*j; converting their signs requires r>0 on the positive half-line and the stated extensions. No claim of identical expression or extracted dependency is made.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. The concrete Lean finite-data integration uses gaussian_shape_coercivity on the positive half-line, not a raw instantiation of the generic whole-line helper; the accompanying citation relation records the representation difference at zero.

Only derivative moments through order four pass to the limit, with one further derivative bound for path evaluation; no density-score convergence is asserted. The c=0 case is separate.

Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Unconditional with respect to minimization; conditional on admissibility and a positive plateau. The cited Lean positive_gap_curvature supplies the positivity of the second derivative of curvatureMoment, not a claim of literal equality between every manuscript lemma and a Lean type.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Pure finite polynomial identity and coefficient comparison. Analytic signs, density, integration, approximation and strictness are separate nodes. The explicit coefficients are source-bound rather than redefined in a second store; inspection of a Lean proof ending in ring does not report a replay.

Curated source-level mathematical statement, not an elaborated Lean extraction or independently accepted proof. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. Source-level analytic leaf package. Heat-semigroup estimates, control-value stability, interpolation and Gronwall are supplied in the cited proof but not individually represented. There is no uniform spatial-derivative bound up to terminal time 1. No minimizer hypothesis is needed.

Fixed finite-step smooth-terminal data only; constants may depend on these data. This leaf includes heat-kernel construction and Gaussian convolution estimates. Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. The boundary-layer estimate itself does not use minimality. It uses the finite plateau and terminal cusp, not a derivative estimate uniform up to time 1. Constants depend on the fixed coefficient/plateau; no quantitative bound uniform over minimizers is claimed.

Its displayed local hypotheses are quantified guards; a hypothetical plateau is not an added premise of the full-support theorem. No division by c and no appeal to the positive-plateau certificate. For an initial interval (0,b), apply the assertion locally at each t>0 and use continuity at 0 for the final integration.

support_boundary.meaning: Not mapped as a claim means absent from the selected passages' claim_ids, not absent from their prose. The whole-passage boundary treats explicitly mapped assumptions as roots, alongside recorded prerequisites; it is not a list of undischarged premises for each individual claim. No sentence-level explanation coverage is inferred.

paper_scope.meaning: Authored focus; mentioned claims and retained prerequisites may extend beyond these goals.

coverage.citation_audit_scope: Recorded documentary references only; missing effective citation IDs do not establish a mathematical or editorial verdict.
coverage.heading_syntax: ATX headings only; Setext and HTML headings are not parsed
coverage.scope: Mapped passages are correspondences, not sentence-level formal support. Section-passage overlaps are document structure, not claim or proof implications. Unmapped text and passages omitted by the selector remain in the validated paper. Graph records outside the selected prerequisite closure remain in the bundle and are not asserted absent. Argument links combine recorded Lean references, curated support, formalization correspondence and explicit assumptions; their SCCs describe only that mixed recorded reachability. Reading order and platform decomposition are separate.

passages.text: The separate circuit theorem in [OpenAI (2026b)][qaoa-manuscript] resolves the eventual-optimality conjecture for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) in [Basso–Farhi–Marwaha–Villalonga–Zhou, §7, equation (7.2)][bfmvz]. The *Long Reasoning Record*, [§8](../long/reasoning-record.md#qaoa-construction), develops its circuit construction and the order of limits. It requires additional arguments beyond full support.
passages.rationale: Reference-only route to the separate eventual-optimality theorem, prior conjecture and long §9. Does not substitute a shortened theorem with lost quantifiers. Full support alone does not supply the construction.

treatments.rationale: Identifies the separate circuit theorem, its earlier conjecture and the long-record destination. This reference-only passage does not replace the quantified theorem or its additional construction with full support alone.

coverage.empty_result_meaning: No matching recorded passage correspondence. An unmapped section may contain mathematics; zero matches do not establish independence or absence of a prerequisite.
coverage.scope: One validated bundle capture. Direct matches use claim_ids and assumption_ids only. Prerequisite matches follow stored Lean, support, formalization and explicit assumption links, retaining each kind; citations, document order and platform decomposition never become premises. Witnesses show one deterministic shortest recorded path, not a proof or complete explanation.
